name: Pul
title: Assyrian king who invaded Israel
summary: Pul is the biblical name for Tiglath-Pileser III, the king of Assyria who invaded Israel during the reign of King Menahem. Menahem paid a huge tribute of one thousand talents of silver to secure Assyrian support and keep his throne. Pul played a crucial role in the Assyrian expansion that eventually led to the fall of the Northern Kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Invasion of Israel
keyEvents.description: Pul (Tiglath-Pileser III) came against the land of Israel with his army, and King Menahem had to pay him one thousand talents of silver as tribute to avoid destruction.

keyEvents.title: Tribute from Menahem
keyEvents.description: Menahem collected the silver from all the wealthy men in Israel, fifty shekels of silver from each man, to pay the king of Assyria. Then Pul returned and did not stay in the land any longer.

keyEvents.title: Deportation of the Northern Tribes
keyEvents.description: Tiglath-Pileser (Pul) conquered several cities and regions in Israel, including Ijon, Abel-Beth-Maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, and Hazor, and deported their inhabitants to Assyria.

keyEvents.title: Alliance with King Ahaz of Judah
keyEvents.description: King Ahaz of Judah sought help from Tiglath-Pileser (Pul) against Syria and Israel, and sent him gold and silver from the temple and the king's treasury.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: First Chronicles identifies Pul and Tiglath-Pileser as the same person, and tells how the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of the Assyrian king to carry away the eastern tribes into exile.
